To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the flexoelectric and dielectric effects in liquid crystals are not additive and that the electric field profile in liquid crystals is not a simple superposition of the external and internal fields.
the flexoelectric coefficient of p-pentylcyanobiphenyl is negative, and that the surface polarization is not a constant but depends on the electric field applied to the liquid crystal.

the electric field profile and the molecular orientation inside the nematic liquid crystal are strongly affected by the ions and that these ions are not uniformly distributed along the cell thickness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular orientation of a liquid crystal submitted to a low frequency electric field.
the influence of ions on the molecular orientation of nematic liquid crystals.
the determination of the surface polarization and of the flexoelectrical coefficients of a nematic liquid crystal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the flexoelectric effect and surface polarization in the nematic liquid crystals have not been measured in this experiment.
the experimental results reported by Mazzalla et al. cannot be interpreted as a direct measurement of the flexoelectrical and surface polarization coefficients.
the experimental data of Mazzulla and co-workers are not sufficient to extract the flexoclectric coefficients and the polarization at the surface of the liquid crystal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electric field profile in the liquid crystal is strongly affected by the presence of the ions.
the flexoelectric effect in nematic liquid crystals cannot be considered as a pure molecular effect but is also related with the ionic polarization.
the experimental determination by Mazzulla of the flexoelectricties and surface polarization of the liquid crystal is not correct.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the experimental results of Mazzulla are not sufficient to determine the flexoelectric coefficient and the surface polarization.
the flexoelectric and surface polarization coefficients extracted by Mazzulla and co-workers are overestimated by about one order of magnitude.
, for a proper determination of the surface polarization and the flexoelectric coefficient, the ionic contribution to the electric field must be taken into account.
